A 23-year-old male construction worker is brought to the emergency department with acute confusion
after being found unconscious at his worksite. His medical history includes seizure disorder and
schizophrenia, for which he takes haloperidol. He underwent an appendectomy two months ago. On
examination, his vital signs show: temperature 105.1°F (40.6°C), blood pressure 125/69 mmHg, heart
rate 150/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. The patient is confused
and non-communicative, with sweat-soaked clothing. While he shows no clear focal neurologic deficits,
he lacks purposeful movement of his extremities. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices:
(A) Anticholinergic toxicity (B) Exertional heat stroke (C) Malignant hyperthermia (D) Neuroleptic
malignant syndrome (E) Central nervous system infection (F) Drug-induced hyperthermia (G) Septic
shock (H) Nonexertional heat stroke (I) Thyroid storm (J) Status epilepticus
 A. Drug-induced hyperthermia
B. Thyroid storm
C. Status epilepticus
D. Central nervous system infection
E. Anticholinergic toxicity
F. Malignant hyperthermia
G. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
H. Exertional heat stroke
I. Septic shock
J. Nonexertional heat stroke
